entity.name: Otto von Bismarck
entity.description: The Iron Chancellor who unified Germany through three wars. A Junker landowner who spoke six languages and mastered Realpolitik, Bismarck provoked conflicts with Denmark, Austria, and France to forge a new empire — then kept the peace for two decades through sheer diplomatic cunning. He also invented the welfare state, not out of compassion, but to undercut the socialists.

story.name: Otto von Bismarck
story.description: A Junker landowner provokes three wars to unify Germany, creates the world's first welfare state to outmaneuver socialists, dominates European diplomacy for 20 years, then gets fired by a 29-year-old Kaiser.

moments.name: Otto von Bismarck Is Born into the Prussian Junker Aristocracy
moments.subtitle: A future empire-builder arrives at a rural estate west of Berlin
moments.description: On 1 April 1815, Otto Eduard Leopold von Bismarck was born at Schönhausen, a noble family estate in Prussian Saxony west of Berlin. His father was a Junker landowner and former military officer; his mother was the well-educated daughter of a senior government official. The boy grew up speaking six languages and studied law at Göttingen and Berlin, but a university friend described him as a reckless eccentric. Bismarck would spend his twenties running the family estate and chasing English women before entering politics at 32 — and reshaping the map of Europe within two decades.

moments.name: Bismarck Declares Germany Will Be Unified by "Blood and Iron"
moments.subtitle: A new minister president tells Parliament that speeches and votes will not settle the great questions
moments.description: On 30 September 1862, newly appointed Prussian Minister President Otto von Bismarck addressed the Budget Commission of the Prussian parliament in Berlin. He declared that the great questions of the day would be decided not by speeches and majority votes but by "blood and iron." The speech was a deliberate provocation — Bismarck was signaling his intent to bypass parliamentary opposition and expand the Prussian army. Within eight years, he would make good on the promise, provoking three short wars against Denmark (1864), Austria (1866), and France (1870) that unified the German states under Prussian leadership.

moments.name: Bismarck Proclaims the German Empire in the Palace of Versailles
moments.subtitle: The ultimate humiliation: a new empire declared in France's most sacred hall
moments.description: On 18 January 1871, in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, King Wilhelm I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor while French forces still held out in besieged Paris. Otto von Bismarck had engineered the Franco-Prussian War specifically to rally the independent South German states behind Prussia, and the gamble worked. The ceremony unified 25 German states into a single empire of 41 million people, making it the most powerful nation in continental Europe. Bismarck chose Versailles deliberately — the act of founding Germany in France's grandest palace was a calculated insult that France would remember for decades.
moments.address: Hall of Mirrors, Palace of Versailles, France

moments.name: Bismarck Creates the World's First National Welfare State
moments.subtitle: The arch-conservative invents social insurance — not to help workers, but to outflank socialists
moments.description: Between 1883 and 1889, German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck pushed through three landmark laws establishing health insurance (1883), accident insurance (1884), and old-age pensions (1889) for German workers. These were the first national social insurance programs in history. Bismarck's motivation was openly cynical: he wanted to bind workers to the state and undermine the appeal of the Social Democratic Party. The strategy partially worked — German socialism survived but moderated. More importantly, Bismarck's welfare model spread across Europe and became the template for the modern social safety net in dozens of countries.

moments.name: Kaiser Wilhelm II Fires Bismarck After 28 Years of Power
moments.subtitle: A 75-year-old Iron Chancellor is dismissed by a 29-year-old emperor he helped crown
moments.description: On 18 March 1890, Kaiser Wilhelm II forced Otto von Bismarck to resign as Chancellor of Germany after nearly three decades in power. The 29-year-old emperor wanted to rule personally and resented Bismarck's domineering style. Bismarck, 75, had no choice but to comply. The British magazine Punch captured the moment in a famous cartoon titled "Dropping the Pilot." Bismarck retired to his estate at Friedrichsruh near Hamburg, where he spent his remaining years writing bitter memoirs. Without Bismarck's diplomatic finesse, Germany drifted toward the alliance system that would produce World War I within 24 years.
